name: Luxury Editorial
visualIdentity: Explicit direction: one focal subject, refined display typography, concise copy, generous negative space, selective image crops and restrained color. Material highlights are sparse; avoid excessive gold, sparkle and blur. Suitable for video or HTML when a premium, editorial presentation fits.
suitableUses: Strongest alone for fashion, hospitality, invitations and premium product reveals; also product/editorial introductions and explanatory or illustrated narratives. These are suggested fits, not exclusive rules. Use chaptered storytelling only when the subject benefits from meaningful stages.
limitations: May feel overworked when the subject needs simultaneous comparison, long reading or dense detail. Keep essential subject features in frame and allow reading time. Avoid obscuring causal links, unexplained scene changes, conflicting progress drivers, exposed image-layer edges and motion that breaks continuity or loops.
palette: Suggestion for new artwork only: background ivory #F4EFE7, foreground dark brown #29251F, subordinate taupe #817159; three discrete tokens, no gradient. Exact task, brand and approved reference colors and their roles take precedence; preserve source image colors and style color families. Taupe with ivory fails the stated 4.5 normal-text contrast target, so reserve it for decoration. Check actual composited text.
motionAndInteraction: Favor slow smooth camera moves, limited parallax and precise settling; preserve cuts and reading holds when useful. One camera move per scene is suggested for the parallax hybrid. HTML may use reduced-motion-aware scroll parallax or scroll-linked story/chapter states; reverse progress should restore matching states. Card tracks need bounded snap selection and keyboard/button alternatives. Video must use deterministic, seekable composition time, not live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements; leave room for reading and speech. Assemble and synchronize authorized assets, then check intelligibility, balance, clipping and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Use loaded fonts, measured spacing and image masks. Select crops with negative space for type; preserve faces, labels, product details and motion margins. Optional Cropper.js prepares non-destructive crops; it does not create cutouts, parallax layers or missing artwork. Use PhotoSwipe only for an actual interactive image lightbox, with dimensions, alternatives and accessible navigation.
combinations: Best alone. Optional style-052 letterpress for title moments: shallow deboss, dark-brown impression, taupe only for a rule or monogram; avoid metallic bevels, deep emboss and glitter. Optional style-101 adds two or three supplied-image planes with minimal parallax; no generated fill, heavy blur or exposed edges. Motion references are optional: chapter handoffs and story states when narrative supports them; card carousel for concise sequences; curved gallery only for actual images and captions. A flat track is a simplification, not curved-gallery fidelity.
productionApproach: HTML/CSS and SVG are the recommended visual tools; Motion is optional, while GSAP is the seekable timeline route when synchronization is unestablished. HyperFrames is primary for composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation and export; Remotion only for verified HyperFrames unavailability or limitation, with reason recorded. Keep visual construction and motion in their own layers, one owner per animated property. Load assets, seed randomness, inspect key frames and full output. Interactive controls belong to HTML; video state must remain deterministic.
